reuses_without_rewriting: m7-head-issue-v1 (ADR 0035 design philosophy, blinding pattern, isolated claude_cli backend, non-authority disposition contract)
m7-local-factorial-v3 (frozen execution condition, candidate schema, ADR 0037 extraction contract, failure-class taxonomy)
question: does ReviewGraphen with qwen3.8:27b-mlx surface findings on live, previously-unexamined fsl HEAD code that a cross-family judge would plausibly want tracked, and does the ReviewGraphen scaffold change this relative to unscaffolded qwen (B1)

target.ground_truth: none — this is undiscovered-defect search on live code, not known-target re-detection

units.algorithm_summary: global lexicographic file order under rust/*/src (excluding rust/spikes and tests/), greedy 120000-byte packet packing, 4 single-files-over-cap excluded and disclosed, 9-of-31 packets chosen by fixed-stride systematic sampling packet_index(i)=floor(i*31/9)

qwen_b1.description: qwen3.8:27b-mlx given the unit's raw source files only, no ReviewGraphen scaffold
qwen_b1.role: baseline comparator; required so 'is ReviewGraphen useful' has an answer, not just 'does qwen find anything'

qwen_full.description: qwen3.8:27b-mlx given the unit's raw source files plus the standard ReviewGraphen review scaffold
qwen_full.scaffold_construction: reuses the existing full_reviewgraphen packet-construction path used for m7-local-factorial-v2/v3 (arm b1_free_form vs full_reviewgraphen), adapted to build fresh packets from the units in units.json instead of the frozen m7-real-v1 corpus; exact adaptation is an implementation detail finalized and smoke-tested (see execution.smoke_test_required) before the first real generation call, and must not change unit file sets, the candidate schema, or ADR 0037 extraction
qwen_full.role: primary arm of interest per the operator's stated research question

arms.extraction_contract: unchanged ADR 0037 (docs/adr/0037-candidate-json-extraction-contract.md): fenced-block-first, then left-to-right first JSON object, no repair or normalization
arms.candidate_schema: unchanged reviewgraphen.benchmark.candidate_output.v1 (same schema as m7-local-factorial-v2/v3); obligation_results is expected to be an empty array for every trial in this experiment, since no obligations are declared for open-ended discovery
arms.scoring: reviewgraphen-benchmark's 'validate candidate' (schema check) is reused unchanged; 'collect' (scoring against a private oracle) is NOT used anywhere in this experiment because there is no oracle — findings are counted and passed to the judge, never mechanically scored for detection

generation_execution_condition.backend: LM Studio behind cch, endpoint http://192.168.68.71:11999 only
generation_execution_condition.note_on_reasoning_effort: does not suppress reasoning on this backend (observed in m7-local-factorial-v3); retained anyway for continuity with the frozen v3 condition, not because it is expected to work
generation_execution_condition.sampling: provider default, unmodified — temperature/top_p never overridden
generation_execution_condition.amendment_required_to_change: any change to this block after seeing any m7-head-local-v1 result requires a dated, committed amendment before the next call, per the discipline already applied throughout m7-local-factorial-v3

judge.backend: claude_cli via reviewgraphen-benchmark run-process-reviewer claude (generic isolated backend, distinct from the codex-profile adapter)
judge.blinding_mechanism: JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 2-4: content-hash finding_id excluding arm/generator/local_id, hash-sorted pooling across both arms per unit, --no-session-persistence, --tools "", forbidden-marker scan before packet construction
judge.authority: non-authoritative model disposition only, per ADR 0035; never itself creates an upstream object

execution.trial_order: units in unit_index order 0..8; within each unit, qwen_b1 before qwen_full; strictly sequential (one provider request in flight at a time), matching the concurrency=1 decision recorded in m7-local-factorial-v3 PARALLEL2_REVERT_AMENDMENT.md
execution.judge_calls: at most 9 (one per unit), skipped for any unit whose pooled finding set is empty (JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 2.4)
execution.smoke_test_required: one synthetic-input smoke test of the claude_cli judge backend (JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 8) must complete and be recorded before the first real judge call; this backend has never been exercised end-to-end in this repository
execution.failure_taxonomy: unchanged from m7-local-factorial-v3 STAGE1_STATUS_SUMMARY.md: valid, candidate_schema_invalid, empty_final_after_process_completion, upstream_server_stream_incomplete (subtype upstream_model_crash), upstream_server_unresponsive, client_idle_timeout, operator_terminated, infrastructure
stop_conditions: control endpoints respond but a generation or judge request never returns
operator redirect, recorded the same way m7-local-factorial-v3 cell 3 was recorded
execution.not_a_stop_condition: elapsed time alone; m7-local-factorial-v3 observed single trials completing successfully after more than 45 minutes and running past 85 minutes before failing, so duration alone is not evidence of a problem

completion_rate_tracking.unit_of_record: per (unit, arm) generation trial and per (unit) judge call
completion_rate_tracking.explicit_hypothesis_carried_from_v3: m7-local-factorial-v3 STAGE1_STATUS_SUMMARY.md section 4.4 observed one B1 trial exhaust its entire output budget on reasoning with zero final content (85.8 minutes) while the paired full_reviewgraphen trial on the same unit completed quickly (13.4 minutes, 23% of budget) and validated. This is an unconfirmed n=1 observation, not a claim. m7-head-local-v1 tracks per-arm completion rate explicitly so this can be checked with up to 9 more paired observations; a low qwen_b1 completion rate is itself a reportable result, not a nuisance to be explained away.

reported_metrics: generation completion rate per arm (fraction of 9 trials reaching valid schema-conformant output)
raw_findings_count per arm across all units (secondary metric only — inflated by within-arm and cross-arm near-duplicate repetition, see JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 7)
distinct_count per arm (clustered, JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 7): number of distinct underlying claims that arm raised, correcting for repetition
redundancy_ratio per arm = raw_findings_count / distinct_count (higher = more repetitive)
issue_should_be_created count and fraction per arm, both raw and clustered
should_not_be_created and unable_to_determine counts per arm
quality-rubric distribution per arm (specificity, unresolvable_location, reproduction_conditions_stated, false_positive_suspected, design_intent_confusion_suspected)
unresolvable_location_count and rate per arm (raw finding level; a hallucinated-location rate distinct from vagueness, see JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 7)

distinct_issue_worthy_count per arm (JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 7, cluster-level high_confidence_cluster credited to every contributing arm) — this is the PRIMARY count-based metric; the equivalent raw (unclustered) finding-level count is reported alongside it, never in place of it
cross-arm finding overlap (both the pre-clustering byte-identical collapse, JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 2.1, and the judge-asserted duplicate clusters that span both arms, section 7)
per-unit breakdown table (unit, arm, completion outcome, raw finding count, cluster membership, disposition tally)

usefulness_determination.status: descriptive synthesis, not a binary pass/fail gate — consistent with this benchmark family's existing analysis philosophy (m7-local-factorial-v2 preregistration.json 'analysis': descriptive, no significance claim)
usefulness_determination.predetermined_reporting_rule: qwen_full is reported as showing more evidence of usefulness than qwen_b1 only if, after generation and blind judging complete: (a) qwen_full's generation completion rate is not lower than qwen_b1's, AND (b) qwen_full's distinct_issue_worthy_count (cluster-based, JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 7 — NOT the raw finding-level count) is higher than qwen_b1's, AND (c) qwen_full's false_positive_suspected rate among issue_should_be_created findings is not substantially higher (defined as not more than 15 percentage points higher) than qwen_b1's. If these do not all hold, the report states which held and which did not, without averaging them into a single verdict. If either arm's completion rate is near zero, the report states plainly that this experiment could not evaluate usefulness for that arm and says so rather than reporting a misleadingly precise quality comparison over a tiny surviving sample.
usefulness_determination.why_distinct_not_raw: raw finding counts reward an arm for repeating the same underlying claim in different words rather than for finding more distinct problems; m7-real-v1 observed B1 producing roughly 6-8x more raw findings than full_reviewgraphen (115 vs 14-17) while judged-valid rates per finding were similar, so an unclustered count comparison in m7-head-local-v1 would very likely just reward whichever arm is more repetitive, not whichever arm found more real problems. distinct_issue_worthy_count is defined precisely to remove this bias; see JUDGE_PROTOCOL.md section 7.
usefulness_determination.reported_regardless_of_the_rule_above: absolute issue_should_be_created counts and rates for each arm (both raw and distinct) are always reported, since a near-zero count for both arms is itself informative about whether local qwen+ReviewGraphen finds anything worth a maintainer's attention on live code, independent of the b1-vs-full comparison. redundancy_ratio per arm is also always reported as an independent finding about generation behavior, regardless of which arm 'wins' on distinct_issue_worthy_count.
usefulness_determination.not_claimed: statistical significance, verified-defect counts, or generalization beyond the 9 selected units

known_limitations: no ground truth: issue_should_be_created is a judge disposition, not a verified defect; recall cannot be estimated

single judge, single model family (Claude, opus, high effort); no calibration pass has been run because there is no known-defect calibration set for live-HEAD findings (unlike ADR 0035's matched-pair calibration, which m7-head-local-v1 does not attempt)

qwen (generator) and Claude (judge) are both LLMs; cross-family judging reduces but does not eliminate correlated error, and the judge's own competence at reading unfamiliar Rust/FSL code is itself unverified here
n=9 units is an exploratory sample, not powered for any significance claim; see UNIT_SELECTION.md for coverage limits
4 files (including the single largest file in the workspace) are excluded from scope entirely by the oversize rule
the claude_cli judge backend has never been exercised end-to-end before this experiment (see execution.smoke_test_required)

generation completion rate is expected to be low based on m7-local-factorial-v3 (0/3 natural-conclusion requests reached final content under the identical execution condition before this experiment's redirect); m7-head-local-v1 may yield very few or zero judged findings per arm, and that is itself a reportable result about local-LLM operational feasibility, not a failure of this design
